reason: The kidney blood sample and nephron preparation visibly provide the blood and filtering unit needed to begin following filtration.
expectation: The nephron will filter fluid and small dissolved substances from the blood.

effect: The sample has been filtered into the tubule, leaving blood cells and most proteins in the vessels; recovery is the next step.
reaction: The distinction between small filtered substances and retained blood components is clear.
reason: Selective tubule transporters are positioned to recover useful dissolved substances from the filtered sample.
expectation: The transporters will return useful dissolved substances from the tubule toward the blood.

effect: The tubule has recovered glucose and other useful substances; water recovery remains to be followed.
reaction: The qualification that almost all filtered glucose is normally recovered is helpful.
reason: The water-permeable tubule is shown returning water toward blood, making it the natural next step.
expectation: Water will move from the tubule fluid toward the nearby blood vessels.

effect: Water has returned toward the blood, leaving wastes in the tubule; the remaining fluid needs a drainage route.
reaction: The sequence from filtration to recovery is straightforward.
reason: Urinary drainage connects the kidney's collecting passages to the route out of the kidney.
expectation: The remaining tubule fluid will enter the urinary drainage route as urine.

effect: Urine now flows to the bladder, completing the filtration and recovery goal. The urinary organs still need connecting to the body.
reason: The kidney pair has a named ureter slot, and the ureters connect the kidneys toward the bladder.
expectation: The ureters will fit into the kidney pair's drainage route.

effect: The ureters are fitted to the kidneys; the bladder slot remains.
reason: The bladder is the remaining named fitting for the kidney pair.
expectation: The bladder will attach to the ureters as part of the urinary organ assembly.

effect: The kidneys, ureters and bladder are assembled; they still need connecting to the body.
reaction: The drainage route is clear and the fitting worked as expected.
reason: The remaining goal is to connect the assembled urinary organs to the body.
expectation: The urinary organs will connect to the body's circulation and overall model.

effect: The kidneys are now connected to the body's circulation, with ureters leading to the bladder; both chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The final connection was predictable and brought the two construction sequences together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following filtration and recovery was most worthwhile: the planned pictures distinguish substances retained in blood from filtered glucose and water returned to it.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the ureters and bladder was clear but repetitive after the drainage route had already been shown.

surprise.text: The statement that healthy kidneys normally recover almost all filtered glucose sharpened my understanding of how selective recovery is.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless, though the separate drainage demonstration and organ fittings partly repeated the same route.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for more connections between organ systems, although this chapter's straightforward fittings were less engaging than its filtration sequence.
